generation.scope: For a reduced twenty-point finite window with full middle support, different marked four-spaces spanning a five-space force an opposite symmetry. A ruling cannot supply thirteen common-kernel pencils. For a plane conic the off-plane rank-one points and transverse contacts are controlled by one binary quadric. Projecting from its at most two distinguished points gives three independent opposite words supported on at most two points. The identically zero quadric yields a second conic or a symmetric matrix space. Consequently reduced finite rank ten has an opposite symmetry and reduced finite rank eleven is impossible under full middle support.

open_mathematics: Analyze the reduced one-symmetric rank-ten case with unequal symmetric triples (g=4 or 5), using eigenlines and opposite square interpolation. Extend the five-space theorem beyond reduced twenty-point graphs; continue rank-ten four-support branching pencils.
